alignments.note: Indefinite τις → any man; head on any, man being the supplied generic completion (rules 17, 69).
Bare thinketh; the supplied complementizer goes to the expanded non-finite complement under rule 85.
The perfect infinitive is expanded into a finite clause: the complementizer that (rule 85) and the supplied subject he (rule 74) are its helpers, headed on the lexical verb.
ἔγνω takes its supplied subject; head on the lexical verb.

οὔπω → not yet, one adverb over two English words. Head on yet rather than not: rule 17 forbids choosing a word merely because it stands first, and yet is what distinguishes this lexeme from a plain οὐ. A head on not remains defensible.
Impersonal δεῖ recast with a personal subject; head on the lexical modal ought.
Bare infinitive with no governing conjunction, so the infinitival to is its own verb's helper (rules 7, 61).

review_notes: v001, v002 and v004 are underdetermined with the projection carrying r00-base, which the English permits; no textual decision is taken here (rule 12).
The head of οὔπω is the one genuinely open choice in this verse and the note on that unit names the competing reading.
